List of Pokémon Trading Card Game expans:
This is a list of English [[Pokémon card]]s from the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]] expansions. For Japanese sets, see the list of [[List of Japanese Pokémon Trading Card Game expansions|Japanese Pokémon Trading Card Game]] expansions. Prior to the EX Series, expansions were distributed by [[Wizards of the Coast]]. '''WIP''' {{redirect|SVI|the Japanese set number using this abbreviation|Pokémon Card Game Battle Academy (TCG)}} {{ExpansionPrevNext|prev=Crown Zenith|next=Paldea Evolved}} {{TCGExpansionInfobox |setname=Scarlet & Violet |setsymbol=yes |alt=Scarlet and Violet |setlogo=SV1 Logo EN.png |cards=258 |setnum=95 |release=March 31, 2023 }} '''Pokémon TCG: ''Scarlet & Violet''''' is the first main expansion of cards from the Scarlet & Violet Series of the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]]. It was released on March 31, 2023. ==Blurb== Begin a New Adventure with Pokémon ex! Set out for a journey in the Paldea region! Meet first partners Sprigatito, Fuecoco, and Quaxly, and explore the power of the Legendary Pokémon Koraidon and Miraidon as Pokémon ex. Other Pokémon ex evolve their way into battle—including Arcanine and Gyarados with a dazzling new look. Even more Pokémon appear as illustration rare cards with amazing artwork—discover them all in the Pokémon TCG: Scarlet & Violet expansion! ==Information== Scarlet & Violet focuses on {{p|Koraidon}} and {{p|Miraidon}}, both of which are included as {{TCG|Pokémon ex}}. This set marks the introduction of {{TCG|Pokémon ex}} and is the first to feature Pokémon, items, characters and places from the {{g|Scarlet and Violet}} games. Certain Pokémon ex also include a new '''Tera''' (Japanese: '''テラスタル''' ''Terastal'') mechanic, based on the [[Terastal phenomenon]] from the Scarlet and Violet games, which prevents damage done to those Pokémon by attacks while they are on the {{TCG|Bench}}. This new expansion introduces various design changes for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. For international audiences, yellow borders on Pokémon TCG cards have been changed to gray to match the cards released in Japan. Additionally, expansion symbols are replaced by expansion codes and language codes across all cards. All cards with a Rare [[rarity]] are [[holofoil]] in {{TCG|booster pack}}s, and booster packs now contain a guaranteed three Holofoil cards instead of only two. For worldwide audiences, subcategories for {{TCG|Trainer card}}s — such as Supporter, Item and Stadium — will appear in the top left corner to be more visible in players’ hands. {{TCG|Energy card}}s display another Energy symbol on the bottom right corner to make it easier to track during gameplay.[https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/pokemon-tcg-scarlet-violet-brings-changes-to-the-pokemon-trading-card-game ''Pokémon TCG: Scarlet & Violet Brings Changes to the Pokémon Trading Card 108 (Violet ex) |setnum=88 |release=January 20, 2023 |japrevset=Paradigm Trigger |japrevsetname=Paradigm Trigger |janextset=Snow Hazard/Clay Burst |janextsetname=Snow Hazard • Clay Burst }} '''Scarlet ex''' (Japanese: '''スカーレットex''') and '''Violet ex''' (Japanese: '''バイオレットex''') are the names given to the two Japanese paired sets that collectively make up the first main expansion of cards released during the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]]'s {{TCG|Scarlet & Violet Era}}. ==Information== [[File:SV1S Logo JP.png|200px|thumb|Scarlet ex logo]] [[File:SV1V Logo JP.png|200px|thumb|Violet ex logo]] Scarlet ex and Violet ex focus on {{p|Koraidon}} and {{p|Miraidon}} respectively, both of which are included as {{TCG|Pokémon ex}}. This set marks the introduction of {{TCG|Pokémon ex}} and is the first to feature Pokémon, items, characters and places from the {{g|Scarlet and Violet}} games. Certain Pokémon ex also include a new '''Tera''' (Japanese: '''テラスタル''' ''Terastal'') mechanic, based on the [[Terastal phenomenon]] from the Scarlet and Violet games, which prevents damage done to those Pokémon by attacks while they are on the {{TCG|Bench}}. For worldwide audiences, subcategories for {{TCG|Trainer card}}s — such as Supporter, Item and Stadium — will appear in the top left corner to be more visible in players’ hands. {{TCG|Energy card}}s display another Energy symbol on the bottom right corner to make it easier to track during gameplay.[https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/pokemon-tcg-scarlet-violet-brings-changes-to-the-pokemon-trading-card-game ''Pokémon TCG: Scarlet & Violet Brings Changes to the Pokémon Trading Card Game'' | Pokémon Website] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20221209142252/https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/pokemon-tcg-scarlet-violet-brings-changes-to-the-pokemon-trading-card-game archived copy]) {{TCG|Pokémon Tool card}}s are now considered a category of {{TCG|Trainer card}}s alongside {{TCG|Item card}}s, {{TCG|Supporter card}}s, and {{TCG|Stadium card}}s instead of a sub-category of Item cards. revavroom + garde/koraidon ex gardevoir ex + drifloon dondozo + tatsugiri spidops ex + heracross miraidon ex + pachirisu Scarlet ex and Violet ex were released in Japan on January 20, 2023, followed by localized releases in {{pmin|Taiwan}} and {{pmin|Hong Kong}} on February 3, 2023, in {{pmin|Thailand}} on February 24, 2023, in {{pmin|Indonesia}} on March 3, 2023, and in {{pmin|South Korea}} on March 15, 2023. FLO (TCG): {{Upcoming notice}} {{ExpansionPrevNext | prev = Delta Reign | next = None }} {{TCGExpansionInfobox |setname=FLO |setsymbol=yes |setlogo=None.png |cards=TBD |setnum=111 |release=TBD }} "'''FLO'''" (from its set abbreviation) is expected to be the seventh main expansion of cards from the Mega Evolution Series of the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]]. This set introduces cards of Z [[Mega Evolution]] Pokémon, first introduced in the [[Mega Dimension]] DLC of the video game {{g|Legends: Z-A}}. Details about this expansion, including its name and release date, are currently unknown. ==Information== '''FLO''' is expected to be the seventh main expansion of cards for the Mega Evolution Series of the Pokémon Trading Card Game, introducing Z [[Mega Evolution]] Pokémon from the [[Mega Dimension]] DLC of the video game {{g|Legends: Z-A}} as {{TCG|Mega Evolution Pokémon ex}} cards. Cards in this expansion were first revealed at the conclusion of the [[2026 Pokémon World Championships]] in San Francisco, California, United States. Details about this expansion are currently unknown. As the set's name has not yet been revealed, the set abbreviation "FLO" is used on this wiki as a placeholder. The FLO expansion includes cards released in the Japanese {{TCG|Aura Seeker}} expansion. ==Set list== {{Setlist/header|title=FLO|tablecol={{TCG Fighting color}}|bordercol={{TCG Metal color dark}}|cellcol={{TCG Metal color light}}|rarity=yes|symbol=yes|image=SetSymbolFLO.png}} {{Setlist/entry|032/080|J|{{TCG ID|FLO|Sigilyph ex|32|Sigilyph}}{{ex}}|Psychic||Double Rare}} {{Setlist/entry|045/080|J|{{TCG ID|FLO|Riolu|45}}|Fighting||Common}} {{Setlist/entry|058/080|J|{{TCG ID|FLO|Mega Lucario Z ex|58|Mega Lucario Z}}{{Mega ex}}|Metal||Double Rare}} {{Setlist/footer|cellcol={{TCG Metal color light}}}} {{-}} {{Project TCG notice}} {{-}} {{TCG Releases|MEGA}} [[de:FLO (TCG)]]
Jamboree (TCG):
{{TCGExpansionInfobox |setname=Jamboree |setlogo=PlaysetJamboree.png |setsymbol=no |cards=Unknown |setnum=Unreleased |release=Unreleased |prevset=Skyridge |nextset=EX Ruby & Sapphire }} '''Jamboree''' would have been the last main expansion of cards released by [[Wizards of the Coast]] and was intended to be the first "Wizards' designed" set. However, it was never released. Jamboree's release was prevented by [[The Pokémon Company International|Pokémon USA]] following business disputes over the Pokémon TCG license.[https://web.archive.org/web/20051115123852/http://wizards.com/default.asp?x=company/pr/20030428a RE: Future Pokémon TCG Releases by Wizards of the Coast | Wizards of the Coast], archived November 15th, 2005 ==Information== This set would have been the 17th English expansion had it released. It would have been the first set of cards developed by Wizards of the Coast instead of [[Creatures, Inc.]], and it was to include a mix of {{TCG|Owner's Pokémon}}, {{TCG|Dark Pokémon}}, and cards from the {{TCG|Vending Machine cards|Expansion Sheet}} series of "vending machine promos". Ideas for Jamboree cards included new {{TCG|Trainer card}}s to fix perceived balance issues, previously rejected Pokémon and ''{{wp|Magic the Gathering}}'' card ideas from Wizards, and joke cards with essentially meaningless effects, such as "Flip a coin as many times as you want."[https://www.matobadesign.com/jamboree Pokémon Jamboree ⁠— MATOBA DESIGN] The art for Jamboree would have included original art by Western artists to complement Wizards' original cards. [[User:Nick15|Nick15]], a well-known artist from the Create-a-Card forums, was approached for art. Additionally, many promotional cards that had not yet been released outside of Japan were to be included to catch up Western audiences. The set was first introduced to the public as the Unnamed Wizards Set, which was Jamboree's alpha name. Jamboree was the beta name for the set. However, since the set was never released, a final name was never stated. Multiple {{TCG|theme deck}}s were finished before cancellation; however, their themes and contents are not currently known. ==Set list== The full set list is still unknown. Estimates have around 60 new Pokémon cards with around 12 new Trainer cards. ===Known Cards=== ====Jolteon==== Jolteon was likely designed because [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s staff were chosen to portray [[Lt. Surge]] and [[Vermilion Gym|his Gym]] at [[Tropical Mega Battle]], which led to them developing an affinity for {{TCG|Lightning}} Pokémon. At the time, Wizards of the Coast staff believed that Lightning-based decks were too weak and were looking to strengthen them.[https://compendium.pokegym.net/chatlogs/Chat_2003_06_12.htm Pokemon Chat Report - Thursday, June 12, 2003], question #1952 Jolteon has 60 HP, and its card text reads as follows:

The effect of this card's attack is unknown. It is possible that this card's attack would force the opponent to switch the Defending Pokémon with one of their Benched Pokémon, similar to the effect of {{m|Whirlwind}} on other {{cat|Cards with Whirlwind|cards with the attack}}. The card text for TM Whirlwind reads as follows:
{{Cardtext/Header|type=Colorless}} {{Cardtext/Attack |type=Colorless |cost={{e|Colorless}} |name=Whirlwind |damage= |jname= |jtrans= |namecategory=none |damagecategory=none |effect=Switch }} {{Cardtext/Footer}} ====Bill's Advice==== Bill's Advice is named after two different Bills. The first is [[Bill]], the creator of the [[Pokémon Storage System]], and the second Bill was a customer service representative at Wizards of the Coast, who gave advice to playtesters. The effect of this card is unknown. Mike Boozer of Wizards of the Coast alleged that this card was later officially but secretly released as {{TCG ID|EX Hidden Legends|Steven's Advice|92}} in {{TCG|EX Hidden Legends}}, and that the effects were the same. This was in part due to the "hand size clause" present on Steven's Advice, which is similar to a rule in ''Magic: The Gathering'', a card game designed by Wizards of the Coast.[https://magic.wizards.com/en/rules Rules | Magic: The Gathering], section 402 The card text for Bill's Advice reads as follows:
Legendary Collection 2 (TCG):
'''Legendary Collection 2''' was a name given to a set [[Wizards of the Coast]] intended to release after losing the Pokémon TCG license. However, it was never released.

==Set size==
*Unknown. It is thought it would include the same or a similar number of cards to that of {{TCG|Legendary Collection}}.

==Sequence==
*If the set were released when Wizards stated, it would have been the 16th English Expansion.

==Release date==
*Late Spring 2003
The set was meant to be released after {{TCG|Skyridge}}, but was prevented from being released by [[Nintendo]].

==Trivia==
*Legendary Collection 2 was to follow the same line as the first Legendary Collection, as it proved so popular. It was believed to include an array of cards from the Neo series, along with some Gym cards and one or two Promos.
*Unlike {{TCG|Jamboree}}, which had a lot of material ready for its release, Legendary Collection 2 had little or no advertising or preliminary material. It seems as though Nintendo did not like the idea of Wizards producing another reprint set, so they prevented its release before any extensive plans could be realized.
